questions.question: What kind of "more UI testing" do you want me to do on UI features?

options.label: Write Dusk tests
options.description: For new UI features, add a test in tests/Browser/ following the existing CreditLine* pattern, so the check is repeatable and lives in the suite.

options.label: Broader manual browser checks
options.description: Beyond the happy path: exercise error states, empty states, role/permission variants, and at least one mobile viewport in the leased preview env before handoff.

options.label: Capture screenshots as evidence
options.description: Save before/after screenshots (or just after, for new features) when reporting the work complete, instead of only sharing a URL.

options.label: Check JS console + network
options.description: On every UI-touching diff, drive the page via CDP and fail the verification if there are JS console errors or 4xx/5xx network calls on the affected pages.

questions.question: Should I add Dusk runs to my default "is this done" check for UI work?

options.label: Yes — run relevant Dusk tests
options.description: Before declaring a UI feature done, run any Dusk test whose path overlaps the diff (e.g. credit-line changes → run tests/Browser/CreditLine*). Add new tests when none exist for the feature.

options.label: Only when I ask
options.description: Keep Dusk opt-in; default stays manual browser verification per the existing memory.

transcript_tail.text: what are the ways we can test UI on browser? are we using playright

Short answer: **no Playwright** — this repo uses **Laravel Dusk** (Chrome/Selenium WebDriver) plus a couple of lighter options. Here's the full menu:

## 1. Laravel Dusk (the real browser tests)
- Dependency: `laravel/dusk: ^8.6` in `app1/family-fund-app/composer.json:33`
- Config: `tests/DuskTestCase.php` — boots ChromeDriver on `:9515`
- Tests: `tests/Browser/` (4 suites, all credit-line UI):
  - `CreditLineBorrowingFlowTest.php`
  - `CreditLineNegativeUITest.php`
  - `CreditLineSimulatorUITest.php`
  - `CreditLineUITourTest.php`
- Page objects: `tests/Browser/Pages/`
- Runs with: `docker exec familyfund php artisan dusk`

## 2. Feature tests with HTTP client (Laravel's test framework)
Most UI-adjacent verification lives in `tests/Feature/` — full HTTP requests, asserts on rendered HTML/JSON, no actual browser. Faster than Dusk; doesn't catch JS/Livewire interaction bugs. Run via `bin/test.sh`.

## 3. Manual browser via preview env (what your memory says to do)
The `lease-env` skill leases one of 6 shared pools (`pool0..pool5`), points it at the current branch, and gives you a URL. Combined with the dev auto-login route:
```
http://<pool-host>/dev-login/dashboard?as=fund-admin
```
…you can drive any role through the UI in seconds. Your `feedback_ui_verify_in_browser.md` memory says this is the expected step for UI-touching diffs.

## 4. Ad-hoc curl against `/dev-login/...`
Useful for smoke-checking that a page renders (HTTP 200, no exceptions) without spinning up Chrome — examples in `CLAUDE.md` under "Claude Testing".

---

**Recommendation if you're considering Playwright**: Dusk covers the heavy interactive flows already (credit-line). Adding Playwright would mean a parallel JS/TS toolchain alongside Dusk — worth it only if you want richer trace/video debugging or want non-PHP devs writing browser tests. Otherwise extending the existing `tests/Browser/` set keeps everything in one runner.
